title: Find an element in a device's allocation
starter:
let alloc_offset (stride : int) (d : int) (i : int) : int =
  0
hints: A replicated allocation is the whole buffer, so nothing moves. A shard starts at element `d * stride` of the buffer.
Subtract `d * stride` from `i`. The result is only a place in the allocation when it is at least 0 and less than `stride`.
`if stride = 0 then i else let e = i - d * stride in if e >= 0 && e < stride then e else -1`
explain: A replicated buffer is copied whole, so element `i` is element `i` of every device's allocation. A sharded allocation holds only elements `d * stride` to `d * stride + stride - 1`, so element `i` sits at `i - d * stride`, the subtraction the kernel prints. Anything outside that range was never copied to this device.
